title: People: character and behaviour
about: Collocations for describing what people are like and how they behave: character phrases such as an outgoing personality, a selfish streak and brutally honest, and verb + noun phrases such as keep your word, bear a grudge and throw a tantrum.

parts.title: Your month of birth and your character
More with word, temper and sense of
parts.note: Книга радить пов'язувати нові словосполучення з людьми, яких ти знаєш: хто з твоїх друзів good company, а хто bears a grudge? Так вони запам'ятовуються значно легше. У таблиці — ще кілька поширених партнерів для word (у значенні «обіцянка»), temper (вдача, настрій) і sense of… (риса характеру).

rows: I give you my word: I'll pay you back on Friday.
He broke his word and never came to fix the fence.
a man / woman of his / her word
Ask Olena to help. She's a woman of her word.
Our neighbour has a quick temper, so nobody argues with him about parking.
be in a bad / foul temper
Dad's in a foul temper because his team lost.
Try to control your temper in front of the children.
After six hours in the car, tempers were getting frayed.
She visits her aunt every Sunday out of a sense of duty.
Our new teacher has a great sense of fun.
His sense of honour wouldn't let him keep the wallet he found.

items.pattern: be good / great / excellent company
items.meaning: be pleasant, interesting and fun to spend time with
items.uk: з ним (з нею) приємно проводити час
items.example: My grandad is **good company**: he always has a funny story about his army days.
more: Take Sofia on the trip with you. She's **great company** on long train journeys.
I was tired and quiet all evening, so I wasn't very **good company**, I'm afraid.
items.watchOut: Company тут незлічуване, тому без артикля: She's good company. A good company — це хороша фірма.

items.pattern: have a selfish / stubborn / competitive streak
items.meaning: a part of someone's character that sometimes makes them think only of themselves
items.example: Even my lovely grandad has a **selfish streak**: nobody else is allowed to sit in his armchair.
more: She's a great flatmate, but she has a **selfish streak** and never asks before she uses my shampoo.
Even generous people can show a **selfish streak** when they're tired and hungry.
items.watchOut: «Жилка» в характері — зазвичай streak, а не vein: a selfish / stubborn / competitive streak. Streak — риса, яка проявляється час від часу, а не постійно.

items.pattern: have an outgoing / a warm / a strong personality · be outgoing
items.meaning: a friendly, sociable character: someone who enjoys meeting and talking to new people
items.example: With her **outgoing personality**, Maria made friends on her first day at the new school.
more: Hotel receptionists need an **outgoing personality** and a lot of patience.
My dad's very **outgoing**: he chats to everyone in the queue at the post office.
items.watchOut: «Комунікабельний, товариський» — outgoing або sociable. Communicative про характер кажуть рідко: воно радше означає «охоче ділиться інформацією». Communicable — це «заразний» (про хворобу), а не «комунікабельний».

items.pattern: have a good / great / dry sense of humour · have no sense of humour
items.meaning: the ability to see when something is funny and to make other people laugh
items.example: You need a **good sense of humour** when you go camping in Wales in August.
more: My aunt has a very dry **sense of humour**: you're never quite sure if she's joking.
He's nice enough, but he has absolutely no **sense of humour**.
items.watchOut: «Почуття гумору» — sense of humour, а не feeling of humour. Британське написання — humour, американське — humor.

items.pattern: have a vivid / a lively / an overactive imagination
items.meaning: the ability to picture things very clearly in your mind; sometimes it means you imagine things that aren't true
items.example: Our daughter has such a **vivid imagination** that her bedtime stories go on for hours.
more: With his **vivid imagination**, he was sure every noise in the old house was a ghost.
Don't believe everything Jack says about his weekend. He has a very **vivid imagination**.
items.watchOut: «Жива уява» — a vivid (або lively) imagination, але не a live imagination. Іноді це м'який натяк, що людина вигадує: She has a vivid imagination. «Фантазія» як здатність — imagination; fantasy — це конкретна мрія чи вигадка.

items.pattern: lose your temper (with sb) ↔ keep your temper
items.meaning: suddenly become very angry and show it
items.example: When the builder arrived three hours late, Mum finally **lost her temper**.
more: My usually calm teacher **lost her temper** when someone threw a paper plane at the board.
Try not to **lose your temper** with the kids: shouting never helps.
items.watchOut: Не lose your nerves. Lose your nerve — це злякатися в останню мить. «Нерви не витримали, я зірвався» — I lost my temper.

items.pattern: adverb + adjective: highly intelligent / educated / skilled / successful
items.meaning: very clever
items.example: Pigs are **highly intelligent** animals, cleverer than most dogs.
more: Their eldest son is **highly intelligent**, but he hates doing homework.
She's **highly intelligent** and picked up Spanish in a few months.
items.watchOut: Highly — прислівник, тому highly intelligent, а не high intelligent. Але з іменником — high intelligence.

items.pattern: have a razor-sharp / a sharp mind · razor-sharp wit
items.meaning: the ability to think and understand very quickly and clearly
items.example: At ninety, my great-aunt still has a **razor-sharp mind** and beats us all at Scrabble.
more: You need a **razor-sharp mind** to follow the plot of this detective series.
The quiz champion had a **razor-sharp mind** and answered before the host finished the question.
items.watchOut: «Розум» тут — mind. Reason — це «причина» або «здоровий глузд», тому a sharp reason не кажуть. Razor-sharp перед іменником пишуть з дефісом.

items.pattern: set (yourself) high standards · set high standards for yourself / sb · have high standards
items.meaning: expect a very good level of work or behaviour from yourself or other people
items.uk: ставити високі вимоги, тримати високу планку
items.example: Our football coach **sets high standards**: if you're late for training, you don't play on Saturday.
more: I **set** myself **high standards** at work, so I find it hard to relax.
This bakery **sets high standards** for its bread, and you can taste it.
items.watchOut: «Ставити високі вимоги» — set high standards, а не put high requirements: requirements — це офіційні умови (для візи, для вступу). Також кажуть have high standards.

items.pattern: fiercely loyal (to sb) · fiercely independent / proud / competitive
items.meaning: extremely loyal; ready to support and defend friends or family whatever happens
items.example: Our old dog was **fiercely loyal** and followed Grandma everywhere.
more: Fans of the local team are **fiercely loyal**, even when it loses every match.
Lena is **fiercely loyal** to her friends and won't hear a bad word about them.
items.watchOut: Fiercely тут не означає «люто, зло»: це «дуже сильно, палко». Відданий комусь — loyal to sb, а не loyal for sb.

items.pattern: the best / worst aspect of your personality / character
items.meaning: one part or side of someone's character
items.example: Patience is the best **aspect of his personality**: he never rushes the children.
more: Being stubborn is not the nicest **aspect of my personality**, I admit.
Travelling alone showed me a new **aspect of my personality**: I'm braver than I thought.
items.watchOut: «Риса характеру» — an aspect of your personality / character або a personality trait, але не a line of character.

items.pattern: put others / your family / your children first ↔ put yourself first
items.meaning: think about what other people need before thinking about yourself
items.example: Nurses spend all day **putting others first**, so they need to look after themselves too.
more: Mum always **put** us **first**, even when money was tight.
Sometimes you need to stop **putting others first** and book a holiday for yourself.
items.watchOut: «Ставити на перше місце» — put sb first, без on the first place. Протилежне — put yourself first.

items.pattern: painfully shy / thin / slow / obvious
items.meaning: so shy that it makes life difficult or uncomfortable
items.example: As a teenager I was **painfully shy** and couldn't even order a pizza on the phone.
more: Their new neighbour is **painfully shy** and goes red when you say hello.
The singer is **painfully shy** off stage, which surprises her fans.
items.watchOut: Сором'язливий — shy. Не плутай з ashamed (якому соромно за свій вчинок) і shameful (ганебний).

items.pattern: give the impression of being… / that… · give sb the impression
items.meaning: make people think something about you or a situation, which may not be true
items.example: He **gives the impression** of being strict, but he's actually a very gentle teacher.
more: I didn't want to **give the impression** that I wasn't interested, so I asked lots of questions.
The hotel website **gave the impression** that it was right by the beach. It wasn't.
items.watchOut: Give the impression that… — створювати враження, ніби… А make a good impression (on sb) — справити гарне враження, сподобатися: She made a good impression at the interview.

items.pattern: supremely confident / talented / fit
items.meaning: extremely confident; completely sure of yourself and your abilities
items.example: The ten-year-old walked on stage looking **supremely confident** and sang without any nerves.
more: She seemed **supremely confident** before her driving test and passed first time.
He's **supremely confident** in the kitchen, but he can't change a tyre.
items.watchOut: Supremely — підсилювач, здебільшого для позитивних слів: supremely confident / talented. Confident — упевнений; не плутай з confidential — конфіденційний.

items.pattern: have a tendency to do sth · tend to do sth
items.meaning: often behave in a particular way
items.example: My sister **has a tendency to** exaggerate, so her 'huge' spider is probably quite small.
more: I **have a tendency to** buy too much food when I go shopping hungry.
Our old car **has a tendency to** overheat on long journeys.
items.watchOut: Після tendency — to + дієслово: a tendency to forget, а не a tendency of forgetting. Простіше сказати: I tend to forget.

items.pattern: make a snap decision / judgement
items.meaning: a decision made very quickly, without time to think carefully
items.example: When we saw the sun come out, we made a **snap decision** to drive to the coast.
more: Don't make a **snap decision** about the flat. Sleep on it.
The goalkeeper had to make a **snap decision**: stay on the line or run out.
items.watchOut: «Ухвалити рішення» — make a decision (британською також take), а не accept a decision: accept a decision — погодитися з чужим рішенням.

items.pattern: have / feel a (strong) sense of responsibility (for / towards sb)
items.meaning: the feeling that you must take care of people or do what you should do
items.example: Having a puppy has given our son a real **sense of responsibility**.
more: She often works late because of her strong **sense of responsibility** towards her patients.
A summer job is a good way for teenagers to develop a **sense of responsibility**.
items.watchOut: «Почуття відповідальності» — a sense of responsibility; a feeling of responsibility теж буває, але рідше. А «почуття гумору» — тільки sense of humour, не feeling.

items.pattern: keep your word ↔ break your word · give sb your word
items.meaning: do what you promised to do
items.example: The plumber said he'd come back on Monday, and he **kept his word**.
more: If you promise the kids a trip to the zoo, you have to **keep your word**.
Dad **kept his word** and taught me to drive the summer I turned seventeen.
items.watchOut: «Тримати слово» — keep your word, а не hold your word. «Дати слово» — give sb your word, «порушити слово» — break your word.

items.pattern: keep a secret · be good / bad at keeping secrets · keep sth secret
items.meaning: not tell anyone something that you were told privately
items.example: Can you **keep a secret**? We're getting married in June.
more: My little brother is hopeless at **keeping secrets**: he told Mum what we'd bought her for her birthday.
We **kept** the party **secret** until the very last minute.
items.watchOut: «Тримати в таємниці» — keep sth secret або keep a secret, а не hold a secret. «Видати таємницю» — give away a secret або let a secret out.

items.pattern: bear / hold a grudge (against sb) · bear – bore – borne
items.meaning: keep feeling angry with someone for a long time because of something bad they did to you
items.example: Grandpa still **bears a grudge** against the neighbour who cut down his apple tree in 1998.
more: She's not the type to **bear a grudge**: ten minutes after an argument she's smiling again.
Life's too short to **hold a grudge** over a parking space.
items.watchOut: «Тримати зло, образу» — bear або hold a grudge (against sb), а не keep anger чи keep an offence. Grudge читається /ɡrʌdʒ/, як judge.

items.pattern: keep your temper (with sb) ↔ lose your temper
items.meaning: stay calm and not get angry, even when it's difficult
items.example: The kids were screaming in the back of the car, but Dad somehow **kept his temper**.
more: Nurses have to **keep their temper** even with very rude patients.
I just about **kept my temper** when the delivery came a week late.
items.watchOut: Temper тут — самовладання: keep your temper — зберегти його, lose your temper — втратити. Але have a temper — бути запальним: Careful, he has a temper.

items.pattern: make a fool (out) of sb · make a fool of yourself
items.meaning: trick someone or make them look stupid in front of other people
items.uk: робити з когось дурня, виставити когось дурнем
items.example: The man at the market tried to **make a fool of** me: the 'leather' bag he sold me was plastic.
more: I won't dance at the wedding. I don't want to **make a fool of myself**.
Stop **making a fool out of** your brother in front of his friends.
items.watchOut: Порядок слів: make a fool of me, а не make me a fool. Make a fool of yourself — осоромитися, пошитися в дурні самому.

items.pattern: brutally honest / frank · brutal honesty · to be brutally honest, …
items.meaning: honest in a very direct way, even when the truth hurts people
items.example: Ask my sister about your new haircut only if you want a **brutally honest** answer.
more: To be **brutally honest**, the soup needs a lot more salt.
Kids can be **brutally honest**: my nephew asked me why my nose was so big.
items.watchOut: Brutally тут не про фізичну жорстокість: правду кажуть прямо, не шкодуючи почуттів. To be brutally honest, … — «якщо зовсім чесно…».

items.pattern: hurt sb's / others' feelings · hurt – hurt – hurt
items.meaning: upset someone by saying or doing something unkind
items.example: I didn't go to her party, and I think it really **hurt her feelings**.
more: Tell him the truth, but try not to **hurt his feelings**.
Grandma's **feelings were hurt** when nobody tried her cake.
items.watchOut: Feelings — у множині: hurt her feelings, а не her feeling. Hurt — неправильне дієслово: hurt – hurt – hurt, тому не hurted.

items.phrase: play a joke / trick on sb
items.pattern: play a joke / a trick / a prank on sb
items.meaning: do something to someone for fun, to surprise them or make them look silly
items.example: My kids **played a trick on** me: they glued a coin to the kitchen floor and laughed every time I tried to pick it up.
more: My colleagues **played a joke on** me and hid my chair in the lift.
Uncle Mark loves **playing tricks on** people, so check your shoes before you put them on.
items.watchOut: «Розіграти когось» — play a joke / trick on sb, а не make a joke on sb. Make a joke (about sth) — пожартувати, сказати щось смішне.

items.pattern: can / can't take a joke
items.meaning: not get upset or angry when people make jokes about you or play tricks on you
items.uk: розуміти жарти, не ображатися на жарти
items.example: Don't tease Tom about his cooking. He can't **take a joke**.
more: Luckily, my boss **can take a joke**, so she laughed when she saw the photo.
You have to be able to **take a joke** if you share a flat with five students.
items.watchOut: «Він не розуміє жартів» (ображається) — he can't take a joke. He didn't get the joke — він не зрозумів, у чому смішне.

items.pattern: swallow your pride (and do sth)
items.meaning: do something even though it is embarrassing for you, for example ask for help or say sorry
items.example: After a week of silence, I **swallowed my pride** and phoned my sister to say sorry.
more: He had to **swallow his pride** and ask his parents for money to pay the rent.
If you're lost, **swallow your pride** and ask someone the way.
items.watchOut: «Переступити через себе, через гордість» — swallow your pride, а не step over your pride.

items.pattern: throw / have a tantrum · a temper tantrum
items.meaning: (usually of a small child) suddenly behave in a very angry, uncontrolled way: scream, cry and kick
items.example: Our two-year-old **threw a tantrum** in the middle of the airport because she wanted to carry her own passport.
more: The footballer **threw a tantrum** when the coach took him off.
Sometimes the best thing to do with a child who's **having a tantrum** is to wait calmly.
items.watchOut: «Влаштувати істерику» — throw / have a tantrum, а не make a hysteria. Про дорослого throw a tantrum кажуть із засудженням: поводиться як мала дитина.

items.pattern: lose (your) patience (with sb/sth) · run out of patience
items.meaning: stop being patient and become annoyed or angry
items.example: After forty minutes on hold to the bank, I **lost my patience** and hung up.
more: The teacher never **loses patience** with slow readers.
After three hours of trying to put up the tent, Dad **lost his patience** and booked a hotel.
items.watchOut: «Терпець урвався» — I lost (my) patience або I ran out of patience. Patience — незлічуване, без s. Не плутай з patients — пацієнти: звучать однаково.

items.pattern: come to terms with sth (a loss, an illness, a change, the fact that…)
items.meaning: slowly accept a sad or difficult situation
items.example: It took Dad a long time to **come to terms with** retiring from the job he loved.
more: She's still **coming to terms with** losing her dog.
Moving abroad is hard. You have to **come to terms with** missing family birthdays.
items.watchOut: «Змиритися з чимось» — come to terms with sth (terms завжди в множині). Не reconcile with: reconcile with sb — помиритися з людиною після сварки.

items.pattern: reveal / show your true character ↔ conceal / hide your true character
items.meaning: show what someone is really like, often something bad that was hidden before
items.example: Our landlord seemed friendly, but the argument over the deposit **revealed his true character**.
more: People often **reveal their true character** when they lose at board games.
In job interviews, people often **conceal their true character** behind a big smile.
items.watchOut: «Показати справжнє обличчя» — reveal / show your true character (або show your true colours), а не show your real face. Протилежне — conceal / hide your true character.

warmup.uk: Мій тато зовсім не розуміє жартів.
warmup.q: My dad can't ___ a joke at all.
warmup.explain: Не ображатися на жарти — can take a joke. Get the joke — зрозуміти, у чому смішне.

warmup.q: He promised, and he ___ his word.
warmup.explain: Дотримати слова — keep your word; порушити слово — break your word.

warmup.uk: Діти розіграли бабусю на Перше квітня.
warmup.q: The kids ___ a trick on their grandma on April Fool's Day.
warmup.explain: Розіграти когось — play a trick / joke on sb. Make a joke — пожартувати словами.

warmup.q: The little boy ___ a tantrum in the shop.
warmup.explain: Влаштувати істерику — throw (або have) a tantrum.

warmup.uk: Я вийшов із себе й накричав на нього.
warmup.q: I lost my ___ and shouted at him.
warmup.explain: Вийти з себе — lose your temper. Lose your nerve — злякатися.

warmup.q: She has a great ___ of humour.
warmup.explain: Почуття гумору — sense of humour, а не feeling.

warmup.uk: Бабуся так і не змирилася з тим, що продала будинок.
warmup.q: Grandma never ___ to terms with selling her house.
warmup.explain: Змиритися з чимось — come to terms with sth.

warmup.uk: Він досі тримає зло на сусіда.
warmup.q: He still bears a ___ against his neighbour.
warmup.explain: Тримати зло на когось — bear (або hold) a grudge against sb.

A.q: Our new flatmate is funny and easy to talk to. She's really good ___.
A.explain: Be good company — з людиною приємно проводити час. Без артикля: a good company — це фірма.

A.q: Let's not rush. I don't want to make a ___ decision.
A.explain: A snap decision — рішення, ухвалене миттєво, без роздумів.

A.q: He kept looking at his watch and ___ the impression that he wanted to leave.
A.explain: Створювати враження — give the impression (that…). Do the impression не кажуть, а produce an impression — книжне, у розмові так не говорять.

B.q: After failing his driving test twice, Sam ___ his pride and asked his younger sister for tips.
B.explain: Swallow your pride — переступити через гордість і зробити те, що для тебе незручно.

B.q: Six months after the move, Nina has finally ___ to terms with life in the city.
B.explain: Come to terms with sth — змиритися з чимось. Тут Present Perfect: has come.

B.q: I'm losing ___ with the builders: they promised to finish last month.
B.explain: Lose patience можна сказати без your, а temper — тільки з присвійним займенником: lose my temper. Patient — пацієнт або «терплячий».

example.title: My grandpa
example.uk:
З моїм дідусем дуже приємно проводити час. У нього добре почуття гумору, і він обожнює нас розігрувати: минулого Різдва він сховав індичку в гаражі. На щастя, бабуся розуміє жарти.

Щоправда, часом він буває безжально чесним. Коли я спекла свій перший торт, він сказав, що той схожий на цеглину, і образив мене. Я засмутилася, але я не тримаю зла, і за годину ми вже сміялися з цього.

Торік у нього погіршився зір, і йому довелося перестати водити машину. Спочатку він ніяк не міг із цим змиритися й зривався на всіх. Зрештою він переступив через свою гордість і дозволив мені возити його до магазинів. Тепер щонеділі о десятій він уже чекає біля дверей зі списком покупок.
example.en:
My grandpa is [[great company|a1]]. He has a [[good sense of humour|a4]] and loves [[playing tricks on|b1]] us: last Christmas he hid the turkey in the garage. Luckily, Grandma [[can take a joke|b2]].

He can be [[brutally honest|a24]], though. When I baked my first cake, he said it looked like a brick, and he [[hurt my feelings|a25]]. I was upset, but I don't [[bear grudges|a21]], and an hour later we were laughing about it.

Last year his eyes got worse and he had to stop driving. At first he couldn't [[come to terms with|b6]] it and [[lost his temper|a6]] with everyone. In the end, he [[swallowed his pride|b3]] and let me drive him to the shops. Now, every Sunday at ten, he's waiting by the door with his shopping list.
